tasks.notes: Design: schema forms with form_definitions and form_versions (config class on the owner unit), form_publications (transaction class, maker-checker) and submissions (transaction class on the handling unit, case_id nullable without a foreign key). Versions are immutable by trigger (only org_path may change, for unit moves) and by grants; their audit row omits the document (the content hash identifies it). Publishing is always maker-checker (SEC-AC-6), not a flag as in the legacy app. A submission names the version it was filled on, which must be the published one (409 stale_version otherwise). Answers are pruned to the form's value fields, hidden values pruned, validated with form-engine/core: 422 validation_failed with errors[{path,code,message}], paths as the engine writes them (items[2].qty). Kernel error codes only. The field-type list for the API comes from a generated form-engine/core file, checked like form:schema. Forms permissions: form:read for every office (READ_ORG); bureau_admin and unit_admin author (create, update, publish); bureau_admin and unit_head approve; submission:create for records officers; submission:read follows the case column of roles-and-permissions.md. unitRefs moved from parties to kernel/org (shared by both slices). The API bundle check now counts only the npm imports of form-engine/core (re2js added to the API). Reviewer (opus) on 673c59c: 1 high, 6 medium, 7 low. Fixed in the follow-up commit: disabled fields hold their default and read-only computed fields their computed value on the server (settledValues); a non-array section value is dropped; choices are checked against static options; the content's last author cannot approve (documentUpdatedBy → publications.content_by, API + CHECK); answers enter the audit log only as an HMAC; names capped (10 languages × 200), JSON depth 12 and 5000 items, NUL refused (422, not 500); the document limit is 960 KB (under the 1 MiB body limit); every Object.prototype name is a reserved key; a locked read checks scope first (403, as PATCH); the requester can withdraw. Accepted or moved: server scope and remote checks → 0.18a/0.18; unvalidated field types → 0.17; switching a form off or renaming it is metadata, not publication (no second person); a submission racing an approval is pinned to the version it read, which stays valid evidence; a duplicate key (409) shows a key exists elsewhere in the region (keys are not sensitive). The legacy test 'approving a deleted form is refused' became 'approving a switched-off form is refused' (forms are never deleted); 'without approvals every save is published' is dropped by design (always maker-checker).
